title: No Recording? The App Now Speaks It Anyway | vitalii.no
description:
Boytasks runs inside a plain WebView wrapper, not a real browser, so it has none of a browser's built-in speech features. Any sentence that didn't already have a pre-recorded audio clip cached for it just played nothing at all — confusing for a kid who taps a button expecting the app to read it out loud.

Android's native text-to-speech engine is now bridged into the app through a small polyfill, nativeTts.ts, that recreates the same speechSynthesis interface the web pages already call, except it routes to the Android bridge instead of a browser API that was never there. WebView debugging was also enabled so the page's actual behavior can be inspected live while testing.

Before, a phrase without a cached recording was simply silence. Now every phrase gets spoken, cached or not, because the app always has the phone's own text-to-speech voice to fall back on.
